papers.title: Enhancing Titanium Alloys with Fe Microalloying: A Review
papers.abstract: Microalloying strategy can effectively enhance the overall performance of commercial pure titanium and TC4 alloy, expanding their applications in the petrochemical, aerospace, and biomedical fields. Iron, as a β-stabilizing and strengthening element, decreases the β transus temperature and refines as-cast microstructure of pure Ti and TC4 alloy. The effect of Fe microallying on microstructural evolution and performances of pure Ti and TC4 alloy have been summarized and analyzed from the perspectives of the first-principles calculations on the effects of multi-alloying elements on phase transformations, changes in microstructural morphology, variations in mechanical properties and fracture toughness. The strengthening factors of Fe microalloying is 223 MPa/wt.% for pure titanium and 481 MPa/wt% for TC4 alloy, which is resulted from the effective grain refinement and strong hindrance of crack propagation by the Fe-enriched β films at the phase boundaries.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述讨论了Fe微合金化对Ti-6Al-4V（TC4）的影响，但未涉及增材制造工艺或机械/疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a review on Fe microalloying of titanium alloys in general, not specifically on additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V, and does not present any experimental mechanical or fatigue data from AM processes.

summary_zh.motivation: 综述Fe微合金化对纯钛和TC4合金显微组织及性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 从第一性原理、微观组织演变和力学性能等方面总结文献。
summary_zh.result: Fe微合金化通过晶粒细化和β相膜阻碍裂纹扩展实现强化。
summary_zh.validation: 基于文献综述，无新的实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To review the effects of Fe microalloying on the microstructure and mechanical properties of commercial pure titanium and TC4 alloy.
summary_en.method: Literature review covering first-principles calculations, microstructural evolution, and mechanical performance including fracture toughness.
summary_en.result: Fe microalloying provides strengthening of 223 MPa/wt% for pure Ti and 481 MPa/wt% for TC4, attributed to grain refinement and crack propagation hindrance by Fe-enriched β films.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the paper is a review of existing literature.

papers.title: Fabrication and Thermomechanical Processing of Titanium-Based Laminates for Enhanced Performance under High Dynamic Impact
papers.abstract: The trade-off between strength and toughness remains a major challenge in structural materials engineering, especially for titanium-based materials. This study explores the potential of titanium-based laminates for lightweight armor, aimed at improving anti-ballistic properties through the use of layered structures. Titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V (Ti64) was combined with metal matrix composites (MMCs) reinforced with TiC or TiB particles (up to 40 vol%) using two powder metallurgy (PM) techniques. The first approach used press-and-sinter blended elemental powder metallurgy (BEPM) to create the laminates in a single step, while the second involved post-processing via hot isostatic pressing (HIP) to enhance material properties. Both fabrication methods produced laminates that significantly outperformed commercial alternatives in ballistic testing against 7.62 mm armor-piercing bullets. The use of HIP post-BEPM enhances material properties by reducing porosity and increasing hardness, highlighting the complementary nature of these technologies in producing efficient and cost-effective armor materials.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V的热等静压后处理，但采用的是粉末冶金而非增材制造，且聚焦于抗冲击性能而非疲劳/力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: The paper studies powder metallurgy laminates, not additive-manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; its focus on ballistic performance is outside the fatigue/mechanical performance scope of AM post-processing.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决钛基材料强度与韧性的权衡问题，开发轻质装甲。
summary_zh.method: 采用粉末冶金并结合热等静压（HIP）后处理制备Ti-6Al-4V与TiC/TiB增强的层状复合材料。
summary_zh.result: 层状复合材料在7.62毫米穿甲弹测试中性能显著优于商用材料。
summary_zh.validation: 通过弹道冲击实验验证了层状复合材料的抗弹性能。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to overcome the strength-toughness trade-off in titanium alloys by developing layered structures for lightweight armor applications.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V laminates reinforced with TiC or TiB particles (up to 40 vol%) were fabricated using blended elemental powder metallurgy and subsequently hot isostatic pressing to improve density and hardness.
summary_en.result: The fabricated laminates significantly outperformed commercial armor materials in ballistic testing against 7.62 mm armor-piercing bullets.
summary_en.validation: Experimental ballistic impact tests were conducted to validate the anti-ballistic performance of the laminates.
